 Markets Barclays to slash 5,000 jobs in AI efficiency push 
 Published Thu, Oct 22 2026 3:41 AM EDT Updated 32 Min Ago Hugh Leask WATCH LIVE Key Points Barclays plans to cut 5,000 jobs, about 5% of its workforce, as it uses AI and technology to streamline operations.
 Layoffs are expected to fall mainly in support functions, with the bank seeing fewer developer roles.
 Third-quarter pretax profits at the London-listed lender came in at £2.3 billion, with group income at £7.4 billion.
 In this article
 BCS 
 Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT British lender Barclays has revealed plans to cut 5,000 jobs — about 5% of its total workforce — as part of an artificial intelligence-linked efficiency push.
 In its third-quarter earnings statement Thursday, Barclays said it was "structurally reducing the cost base to generate capacity for investment."
 About 60% of the cuts are expected to be in support functions, including developers, according to the earnings presentation, which also noted an outcome was "organisational simplification and technology change efficiency driven by AI."
 watch now VIDEO 8:32 08:32 Barclays CEO outlines the three forces to watch in the bond market Squawk Box Europe Shares in the bank were almost 1% lower by 8:50 a.m. in London (3:50 a.m. E.T.), less than an hour into the trading day.
 Barclays' third-quarter pre-tax profit rose 12% year on year to £2.3 billion ($3.1 billion), matching LSEG-compiled forecasts. Group income for the period was £7.4 billion, below analysts' estimate of £7.61 billion.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Barclays. Net interest income was broadly unchanged at £3.91 billion. Its CET1 capital ratio, a measure of financial solvency, edged down to 14.2% from 14.3% at the end of the second quarter. Return on tangible equity fell to 11.7% from 16.1%.
